clue.text: Making an impression -so striking

definitions.meaning: pressing a mark or design into a surface, as with a die or rubber seal
hitting hard, as in ... on something or a press striking coins

explanation.surface: Someone praises a performer who is making a big impression and looks striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: coin-pressing and franking leave an imprint, and to stamp is also to bring a foot or tool down with force.

clue.text: Keeping a pet in a place fit only for pigs is thoughtless

indicators.note: the pig enclosure holds the pet inside it

parts.words: a place fit only for pigs
parts.note: a sty is a pigpen
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: Housing an animal in filthy quarters is careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatterbrained and forgetful, a British informal word for absent-minded.

clue.text: A copper ring or charm

parts.note: P stands for a penny, a copper coin
a peal is the ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A policeman's ring could be a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer or metal; here it is P, for a penny, once a copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractiveness or allure, the quality of drawing people in.

clue.text: Artistic work it's cheap to reproduce

indicators.note: reproducing remakes the letters of it's cheap in another form

explanation.surface: A piece of art is inexpensive to copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reproduce' rearranges ITS CHEAP; the surface sense fits the answer, a work imitating another style.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece imitating the style of another artist or period, a kind of artwork.

clue.text: A well-known school set up a record

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the school is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A famous school established a sporting record.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something down for reference, a verb synonym.

clue.text: The firm with many graduates stops short

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, read as many
MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A company employing lots of graduates abruptly halts something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops short' reads as a verb phrase, but it is a noun phrase: punctuation marks that make brief pauses.
explanation.definitionFit: In punctuation these marks are brief pauses in a sentence, shorter than full points.

clue.text: Trial resulting from gold transaction

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a deal is a transaction

explanation.surface: A court case arises from a gold sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or testing experience, as in trial by fire.

clue.text: The medico is true maybe, but wet

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: maybe suggests is true could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A doctor claims to be honest but is drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges IS TRUE into ISTURE; 'wet' is the noun, as in out in the wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampness or liquid, the noun sense of wet.

clue.text: Makes notes about erosion, using strong language

indicators.note: the singing word goes round the erosion word

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
wear is gradual erosion

explanation.surface: Someone jots down notes on soil erosion while cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes notes' looks like writing; it means producing musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursing and uttering oaths, profane talk.

clue.text: Fitting pipes new building

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Fitting pipes new building', is cut short: PIPES anagrammed leaves A, O, T of APPOSITE unaccounted for (perhaps 'pipes to a'), and no scan or search gives the full text.

clue.text: These days a bog engenders respect

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of years
mire is wet, swampy ground, a bog

explanation.surface: A modern swamp is said to inspire esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is to look up to them, a synonym pair.

clue.text: As a trailblazer, one wants all-round support

indicators.note: the support word surrounds the other word on every side

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trailblazer needs backing from every side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes first into new territory or ideas, a pathfinder.

clue.text: Grace has got in with a liar, unfortunately

indicators.note: the clue words that follow have the name tucked inside them, carried across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A gracious woman has unluckily become friendly with a dishonest person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a woman's name or a quality; here it is one of the three Graces of Greek myth. 'unfortunately' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology she was one of the three Charites, goddesses of charm and festivity.

clue.text: A catastrophe that will involve sad rites

indicators.note: to involve in its old sense is to twist or entangle, so the letters of the following words get jumbled

explanation.surface: Gloomy ceremonies are bound to lead to a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involve' rearranges SAD RITES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity or great misfortune, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Mount without hesitation when given guidance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the horse word wraps around the hesitation

parts.note: a steed is a horse, a mount
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone mounts a horse without hesitating once guided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Directed or piloted along a course, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: Fly around buffet where there's a variety of fish

indicators.note: the word for fly sits round the outside of the word for buffet

parts.note: to wing is to fly
to buffet is to strike or hit

explanation.surface: Insects swarm round a self-service meal where several kinds of fish are laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' suggests a food spread to match 'fish', but it is the verb meaning strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sea fish of the cod family, common on British menus.

clue.text: Smirk if spirit is shown about the Right

indicators.note: the spirit word goes round the letter for right, enclosing it

parts.note: gin is a distilled spirit
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A politician smirks when booze reveals his views on the political Right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' and 'the Right' suggest a political mood, but they give a drink and a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad smile, which a smirk is a smug variety of.

clue.text: Sense people rowing will encompass agreement

indicators.note: the rowing crew word surrounds the agreement word

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Rowers come to see sense and agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: The board put on weight, due to copious seafood

indicators.note: put on here places the weight word after the board word

parts.note: a plank is a board
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A board of directors gains weight from too much seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The board' looks like a committee; it is a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms that form vast amounts of food for marine creatures.

clue.text: Youngster holding a certain Greek character to be an awful beast

indicators.note: the youngster word holds the Greek letter inside

parts.note: a minor is a youngster
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A child holds a Greek figure that turns out to be a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a mythical figure, fitting the answer, but means a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed monster of Greek myth kept in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: The university may end beer supplies

indicators.note: end here asks for the final letter of the word may

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Students at a college may finally run out of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ivy League university in New Haven, Connecticut.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known American Ivy League institution in Connecticut.

clue.text: See main changes made in the plant

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of see main are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A notice tells visitors to look at the major alterations made in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory to go with 'changes made', but it is a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African garden flower with bright two-lipped blooms, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Like a high-flier getting behind

parts.note: as means like
a tern is a seabird, a flier

explanation.surface: A successful person falls behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests an ambitious person; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for at or toward the back of a ship.

clue.text: Pass comment about the objective

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a mark is a target, an objective

explanation.surface: Someone passes comment on the aim.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe or say something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A river always going in different directions

indicators.note: the always word goes in between the compass letters

parts.note: S and N are south and north, two compass points
ever means always

explanation.surface: A river flows constantly in many directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England.

clue.text: Left, being unpleasant

definitions.meaning: in heraldry and Latin the word means on the left-hand side

explanation.surface: Someone has departed, being a disagreeable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for left-handed gave both the heraldic side and the sense of evil or menacing.

clue.text: Stick a man in the centre .

indicators.note: the word for a man goes inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a fellow in the middle and keep him there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' could be a noun, a rod; here it is the verb meaning adhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold together or adhere, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Land backing up the Spanish Italian agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole of the following run is written upward, reversed

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
si is Italian for yes

explanation.surface: A land supports a Spanish-Italian treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' turns ELSI around.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Collect articles received by a monarch.

indicators.note: the articles are taken inside the letters standing for the king

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A king is handed a set of items to gather up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like objects, but means the grammar words A and THE. GR (Georgius Rex, King George) is seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring things together into one place, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A large number put inside break free — such an adventure!

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed within the word for break free

parts.note: to escape is to break free
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of people are locked up, then make a daring break for freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals give a 'large number' as D, 500.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless or daring exploit, a lively adventure.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation housing an occupant

indicators.note: the shelter word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A temporary shelter has someone living in it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rents and lives in a property, a resident.

clue.text: Produces the family-is on guard

parts.note: to bear is to produce, as a tree bears fruit
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A clan produces offspring while keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on guard' sounds like vigilance, but means literally on a Guardsman: the tall black fur cap worn by British Guards regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall fur cap is worn on the heads of soldiers in the Foot Guards outside Buckingham Palace.
